extracted.intended_audience: aspiring op-ed writers and subject-matter experts seeking to place opinion pieces
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and following up on email pitches to place op-eds in newspapers and other outlets; covers what to include, how to establish credibility, and follow-up etiquette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why now? (news hook / timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why now? What’s the news hook? Why is this worth reading at this moment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the immediate relevance of the idea. Keep in mind shelf life: if the idea is very time-sensitive give an editor a day or less to respond; if it's evergreen, a week or two or more is reasonable. Also listed as an aspect of a successful pitch: Timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why this topic? (reader relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why this topic? Why should people care?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey why the subject matters to the publication’s audience—capture interest and explain the piece’s importance quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why me? (author's authority / credentials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why am I the best one to write this piece?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish credibility by stating only the credentials that are relevant. ‘Conveys expertise’ is listed as an aspect of a successful pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include your idea in a few lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Your idea in a few lines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary up front so editors can grasp the premise immediately. This complements answering 'Why now?' and 'Why this topic?'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paste the finished piece below the pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: The finished piece pasted below your pitch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the full op-ed text in the email so the editor can read the complete piece without requesting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contact information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear contact details so editors can respond or reach you quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be brief and clear
rubrics_metrics.description: A pitch should be brief and clear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the email succinct and easy to scan. 'Brief and clear' is listed as a core aspect of a successful pitch alongside being well written and timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be well written
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grammar, clarity, and professional tone matter; a polished pitch demonstrates seriousness and increases the chance an editor will read the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey expertise / establish credibility quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: How do you establish credibility, capture interest, and convey the immediate relevance of your point of view – quickly and decisively?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use selective relevant credentials and concise framing to show you are the right person to write the piece. Workshops and editor feedback can help refine credibility signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer an unexpected point of view
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A distinctive or surprising angle increases the likelihood an editor will pick up the piece; it's listed as a characteristic of successful pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up when an editor responds
rubrics_metrics.description: Thank your editor. Even if they said 'no.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond courteously to any reply. If an editor says no, thanking them can keep the conversation open; if they publish you, thank them for giving space to the ideas and issues (not merely for showcasing you).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up when there is no response / timing for follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a time limit. Then send a follow-up email to the editor saying that you’d still like to run your piece in their publication, but since the piece is timely, if you don’t hear from them by the end of the day (week, whatever) you will assume they have passed, and you’ll be submitting your op-ed elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and communicate a clear deadline for your follow-up depending on the piece's timeliness. Use the deadline to free you to submit elsewhere if the editor passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not simultaneous-submit to most national newspapers
rubrics_metrics.description: Most national newspapers will not consider your piece if you submit to more than one paper at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting the same op-ed to multiple national outlets simultaneously; follow each publication’s submission policy to prevent disqualification.
